features:
Core Monk features (through level 5) — paraphrased, not quoted, since this repo is public; use the Class Reference panel below for the live SRD text where it's covered.

- Unarmored Defense (1st): AC = 10 + DEX mod + WIS mod while wearing no armor and no shield.
- Martial Arts (1st): unarmed strikes/monk weapons can use DEX instead of STR for attack and damage; roll the Martial Arts die (1d6 at level 5) in place of normal unarmed damage; after taking the Attack action with an unarmed strike or monk weapon, make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.
- Ki (2nd): ki points = monk level (5). Ki save DC = 8 + proficiency + WIS mod. Grants Flurry of Blows (1 ki: two unarmed strikes as a bonus action right after the Attack action), Patient Defense (1 ki: Dodge as a bonus action), and Step of the Wind (1 ki: Disengage or Dash as a bonus action, jump distance doubled that turn).
- Unarmored Movement (2nd): +10 ft speed while unarmored (already folded into Speed above).
- Deflect Missiles (3rd): reaction when hit by a ranged weapon attack, reduce the damage by 1d10 + DEX mod + monk level; if reduced to 0 and the missile's small enough, catch it and spend 1 ki to fire it back (range 20/60, proficient).
- Ability Score Improvement (4th, already applied): +2 to one score or +1 to two, capped at 20.
- Slow Fall (4th): reaction when falling, reduce fall damage by 5 x monk level.
- Extra Attack (5th): attack twice, not once, whenever taking the Attack action.
- Stunning Strike (5th): on a melee hit, spend 1 ki to force a Constitution save or the target is stunned until the end of Nathan's next turn.

Optional Monk features (Tasha's) — only if the table is using them: Dedicated Weapon (2nd, touch a weapon after a rest to treat it as a monk weapon until swapped), Ki-Fueled Attack (3rd, spend 1+ ki on your turn for a bonus-action unarmed/monk-weapon attack), Quickened Healing (4th, action + 2 ki: roll the Martial Arts die + proficiency bonus in healing), Focused Aim (5th, after a miss spend 1-3 ki for +2 to that attack roll per ki spent).

Way of Shadow (subclass, chosen at 3rd level) — stealth- and assassination-focused monk tradition; practitioners are often called ninjas or shadowdancers. Source: Player's Handbook / Xanathar's Guide to Everything (not in the open SRD, so summarized here rather than quoted).

- Shadow Arts (3rd level): spend 2 ki to cast Darkness, Darkvision, Pass without Trace, or Silence with no material components. Also grants the Minor Illusion cantrip.
- Shadow Step (6th level): while in dim light or darkness, bonus action to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that's also dim/dark, then advantage on the first melee attack you make that turn.
- Cloak of Shadows (11th level): while in dim light or darkness, use your action to turn invisible until you attack, cast a spell, or step into bright light.
- Opportunist (17th level): when a creature within 5 ft of you is hit by someone else's attack, use your reaction to make a melee attack against it.
notes:
Catchphrase: "These hands."

Per Moss’s dream (S10): saw his mother murdered by a figure resembling his father as a kid.

Confirmed (S10, via the pipe man’s orb): that father is Dr. Tombs. The rest of the party doesn’t know this yet.

Told Bingus (S9): not interested in "the wish" — wants revenge.

Multiclass leaning (next level-up): Sorcerer, Shadow Magic origin — story reasons win out over Warlock here, since an inherited bloodline (Eyes of the Dark, Strength of the Grave) fits a necromancer father better than a warlock's pact framing. Long-rest slots, so it doesn't pair with Ki as cleanly, but that's the tradeoff.

Backup if Sorcerer doesn't pan out: 2 levels of Fighter for Action Surge + Second Wind — barely dents Monk progression, zero stat investment.

Close-range spell picks (not just the Shadow Magic origin features): Shocking Grasp (cantrip, touch, melee spell attack, shuts down the target's reaction) and Poison Spray (cantrip, 10 ft, save-based backup for when Shocking Grasp whiffs) as the starting pair. Thunderwave (1st level, self-centered push) for when he's surrounded. Long-term goal once he's deeper into Sorcerer: Vampiric Touch (3rd level, melee spell attack, necrotic, heals him for half the damage dealt) — the real echo of Dr. Tombs' necromancy.
